sources.title: GLM-5.3-Flash: How to Run Locally - unsloth.ai
sources.snippet: Run the new GLM-5.3-Flash aka ox-alpha model by Z.ai. GLM-5.3-Flash, also known as ox-alpha, is Z.ai's new 320B parameter (18B active) multimodal open model which outperforms GLM-5.2 across benchmarks and real-world tasks at one-tenth the price. GLM-5.3-Flash also rivals Claude Opus 4.8 on coding and agentic benchmarks.

sources.title: How to Run GLM-5.3-Flash Locally: GGUF, Hardware and Benchmarks
sources.snippet: GLM-5.3-Flash is the first natively multimodal model in Z.ai's GLM-5 series, and the first one that's realistic to run locally: it has 320B total parameters and 18B active per token. This guide covers what the model is, how it performs in the benchmarks, how much memory you'll need to run it, and what your options are for running it today.

sources.title: GLM 5.3 Flash | Dell Enterprise Hub by Hugging Face
sources.snippet: Introduction We introduce GLM-5.3-Flash, the first natively multimodal model in the GLM-5 series. With 320B total parameters and just 18B active parameters, it outperforms GLM-5.2 across benchmarks and real-world workloads at one-tenth the price, while approaching Claude Opus 4.8 on coding and agentic benchmarks.

sources.title: GLM-5.3 | OpenLM.ai
sources.snippet: GLM-5.3 is our latest flagship model for coding and long-horizon tasks. It marks a substantial leap in long-horizon task capability over its predecessor GLM-5.1 and delivers that capability on a solid 1M-token context. It is pure open with an MIT open-source license — no regional limits, technical access without borders.
